2609.32782.title: Learning response-aware patient dynamics for respiratory support
2609.32782.paper_summary: Respiratory support can shape the short-term physiological trajectory of critically ill patients, but patients receiving the same intervention may follow different physiological trajectories. Clinical patient dynamics models typically predict future states from recent physiology and recorded interventions, while physiological change is mainly represented through the predicted future state. We propose a response-aware patient dynamics model that explicitly represents physiological change during autoregressive state updating. The model decomposes predicted physiological change into state-dependent baseline dynamics and respiratory-support-associated deviations, with room air providing a reference for the decomposition. We provide a formal analysis of this reference-anchored formulation. A response pathway encodes the predicted physiological change and uses it to update the latent patient state across the forecast horizon. Across ICU cohorts from two independent institutions, the proposed model achieves comparable overall trajectory prediction to patient dynamics baselines, with more consistent improvements when physiological states are changing.
2609.32782.paper_summary_zh: 呼吸支持可以塑造重症患者的短期生理軌跡，但接受相同干預的患者可能會遵循不同的生理軌跡。臨床患者動態模型通常根據近期生理狀態和記錄的干預來預測未來狀態，而生理變化主要通過預測的未來狀態來表示。我們提出了一個響應感知的患者動態模型，該模型在自回歸狀態更新過程中明確表示生理變化。該模型將預測的生理變化分解為狀態依賴的基線動態和與呼吸支持相關的偏差，並以室內空氣作為分解的參考。我們對這一參考錨定的公式進行了正式分析。一條響應通道編碼了預測的生理變化，並利用它在預測範圍內更新潛在的患者狀態。在來自兩個獨立機構的ICU隊列中，所提出的模型在整體軌跡預測方面達到了與患者動態基線相當的效果，並在生理狀態變化時顯示出更一致的改善。
2609.32782.author: Xiaolei Lu et.al.
